evals.prompt: Review my staged changes — they touch an async payment handler and add a new npm dependency.
evals.expected_output: Scoped parallel multi-perspective review with Concurrency and Dependencies activated, synthesized findings, interactive HTML report
expectations: Resolved to Scoped mode and gathered the staged diff plus full file contents, not just the diff
Activated the Concurrency perspective for async changes and the Dependencies perspective for the dependency change
Launched all applicable review perspectives simultaneously in a single response
Delegated review to specialist agents rather than reviewing directly
Deduplicated findings by location and sorted by severity then confidence
Every reported finding includes file:line, a named consequence, and an actionable remediation
Generated the interactive HTML report from templates/report.html with the __REVIEW_DATA__ token replaced
Computed a verdict (APPROVE / APPROVE WITH COMMENTS / REQUEST CHANGES) and offered next steps

evals.prompt: Review PR 42 — it contains a SQL query built by string concatenation from user input.
evals.expected_output: CRITICAL finding with code example; REQUEST CHANGES verdict
expectations: Surfaced the SQL injection as a CRITICAL severity finding with a named consequence
Included a before/after code example with the CRITICAL finding
Verdict was REQUEST CHANGES given a critical finding
Presented only synthesized output to the user, not raw reviewer messages

evals.prompt: Run a full review of this codebase.
evals.expected_output: Audit mode: orientation + co-change by orchestrator, four parallel phase auditors, measured architecture claims, Contextually Acceptable list, 5 refactors, interactive report
expectations: Resolved to Audit mode (no scoped target given)
Performed Phase 1 orientation and co-change archaeology before launching reviewers
Launched smell, architecture, modularization, and practices auditors in parallel in a single response
Architecture claims cite measurements (dependency arrows, amplification counts, co-change data), not principle citations
Findings lacking a named consequence were demoted to the Contextually Acceptable list rather than reported
Report includes a Contextually Acceptable section with reasoning per entry
Delivered exactly 5 ranked refactors, each tied to a Phase 3/4 measurement with an incremental migration path (no rewrites)
Verdict is a calibrated paragraph stating real risks and real strengths
Generated the interactive HTML report with findings, architecture proxies, accepted list, and refactors

evals.expected_output: Scoped review constrained to the named path; consequence-tested findings only
expectations: Constrained the review to the provided scope instead of auditing the whole codebase
Textbook smells without a nameable victim were filed as contextually acceptable, not reported as findings
